Chapter Eight: The Paradox of Wisdom—Knowing That You Don’t Know
As days went by, the younger man kept turning that conversation over in his mind. Those questions that once felt like roadblocks? Now, they seemed more like open doors—inviting him to think a little deeper, listen a bit more carefully, and maybe even live a little more honestly.
He started to realize something important. The older man’s real strength wasn’t in having all the answers. It was in being honest about what he didn’t know.
And that’s the paradox right at the heart of their exchange. So often, the wisest among us are the ones who understand just how little they actually know. Most people are busy trying to look certain—afraid that saying “I don’t know” will make them seem foolish or weak. But the older man showed the opposite. Real wisdom begins with humility—with the guts to admit, “I don’t know, but I want to understand.”
The younger man started to see this everywhere. In the marketplace, the temple, even at home—everyone seemed to prize certainty above all else. But he also noticed what that certainty cost: missed chances to learn, silent doubts nobody dared to voice, and conflicts that might’ve been avoided if folks had just listened a little more.
Inspired by the older man, he tried something new. When he faced tough questions, he stopped himself from blurting out a quick answer. Instead, he asked more questions, listened more closely, and tried to really see things from someone else’s point of view.
Now, I’ll be honest—it wasn’t easy. Old habits hang on tight, and not everyone liked this new way of talking. But over time, he noticed something changing. His relationships grew deeper. His understanding felt richer. And his sense of purpose? It got a whole lot clearer.
That’s the paradox of wisdom. The more you learn, the more you realize there’s so much you don’t know. Sure, it can feel unsettling. But it’s also freeing. You’re no longer weighed down by pretending. Instead, you open yourself up to real growth.
The younger man saw that humility isn’t a weakness. It’s a strength. It’s the foundation for a life filled with learning, deeper connections, and real meaning.
The older man’s example became a quiet guide. A gentle reminder that searching for truth isn’t about having all the answers. It’s about asking the right questions, being comfortable with uncertainty, and embracing doubt— while keeping your curiosity alive, even when the path ahead isn’t clear.
